content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged brown bear frame. Host frame: the brown bear sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines a european rhinoceros beetle and a brown bear. The head is that of the brown bear, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: brown bear body and legs, with its own dense fur on the face, plain coat, no stripes or spots; from the european rhinoceros beetle, as parts and materials on the brown bear's own body: a head horn grown from the frontal bone of the head, above and between the eyes, out of the covering, which continues from there into the body covering — smooth, glossy dark cuticle, one horn curving upward and back from the head; hard, glossy chitin plates with fine seams in its own colors, grown from the skin as the brown bear's own covering over the crown of the head, neck, shoulders, back, flanks, belly, hips, legs and tail. It replaces the brown bear's dense fur there and conforms to the brown bear's body, each plate sized to the brown bear's own body segments and muscle masses, one plate per segment or muscle mass, joined by flexible cuticle at every joint; the dense fur stops at the covering's edge, and the face keeps the brown bear's own dense fur. The covering follows the body's own shape and bends at every joint. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs and visible breathing openings along the flanks. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Composing hybrid creature image**
I'm planning a single creature with a brown bear silhouette and frame, adding a European rhinoceros beetle horn above the eyes that flows into a smooth, glossy dark body covering while keeping the bear's head, fur, and plain coat clear and uncluttered.
**Researching beetle anatomy**
I'm looking up European rhinoceros beetle details to get the horn shape, chitin plate seams, and flank spiracles right for the bear hybrid illustration.
**Drafting hybrid image prompt**
I'm combining both reference images with a detailed text description to build the final prompt for the hybrid creature image.
**Refining hybrid image prompt**
I'm adjusting the prompt to make the design more integrated and natural, swapping armor for chitin plates and reducing the furry, robotic look on the legs while keeping the spiracles.
